metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.117

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.117
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.117
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, we have your letter from the 11th
from Bath and have been happy to hear that you have been there
for a while (wishing you would remain there for good). Please
dear Hannah, do not worry about Eva. You may {love} believe in my
complete sincerity. We have both the feeling that you are an-
xious if at Ms[?] Klaeffer she feels allright and has sufficient
care. Please be sure that she has and we have been surprised
how much she likes the place, the surroundings and has be-
come attached to her, auntie Olga who is really a superior
person and just the right one to guide and to educate a
child. I feel so profoundly how you, poor Hannah, the more the
separation from your child is going on, become more and
more anxious about her. But remember that she is safe,
that she has excellent care and that we are near, that
my sister in law and others would in any case be at hand
and that she is happy, really as happy as she can be without
you both. We have all so many difficult things before us
that you should overcome your longing (which I under-
stand so deeply) with the consolating thought that her de-
velopment, her health, her life, goes on there without the
dangers at home. I {understand} [?] all your secret sorrows to be so
far away from her but I want to comfort you, that you
may at least be sure that she is in excellent care and the
photos will have shown to you, that she is in splendid
health and spirits.
As to your kind questions: please give Freudenthal
every help which is possible, I am so glad that I am
able to be of any use to the few true friends one
has. It would be opressive for me to think that he

Rückseite der ersten Seite, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
would have to worry about money. It is so important
in those days to have at least not to be obliged to worry
about the daily expenses; please assist him with even larger
amounts than before (there will be soon a new amount
in the bank as some of my investements have been sold by
the treasury) and then there is still Frost, who can help and
from Cassels is my royalty due which I can have any moment.
As to the new power of attorney I shall go Monday or Tuesday
to the Consulate and will ask also, if they can send a
short story directly to Luso[?] for the newspaper (the original
as I dispose here of the translation). I have more prepared
than worked and because we have so much practical things
to order and Lotte has been out of work for some time -
I hope the treatment will be effective. The worst for us is
that we do not see clear, what to do. The others have established
themselves in little houses and started a new life, while we
are not sure, how long we shall stay and how to decide -
will it still be possible to go to Brazil? Will there still
be ships and planes? Perhaps when this letter reaches
you the United States will have already entered the war.
So we wait and waiting is not very appropriate for
concentrated work, but I have not been idle and have
different offers and chances at hand - you must not
imagine, that we are disturbed, we would only like not
to wander from one hotel to the other. But we know
also how grateful we have to be that I can continue
my work. We do not see many people, I am tired of
the monotony of the war - the Jewish - the aff[?] david talk;
with his thousand variations it remains sterile. I even
go not to theatres I feel not the right mood for everything which is amusement
while Europe breaks down under the leak of the heart and while you
and all our friends in England are in daily danger. Yours Stefan

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur. Einige wenige Wörter sind aufgrund der Tinte oder der Schriftführung leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext eindeutig.
